subject: loading data all at once versus loading on demand for shiny app

messages.author: a6f35117e675c51c
messages.subject: loading data all at once versus loading on demand for shiny app
parts:
This is a performance/convenience related question .
I have 2500 weather data files. The user of my shiny app can select/view/plot etc any multiple of weather files. for eg view 4 out of 2500 weather files

Option 1:
Load all the 2500 data files as a list of dataframes
weather.data <- list("df1" = df1, "df2"= df2, ... "df2500" = df2500)
weather.data is now ~2GB in size according to Rstudio. I can saveRDS it and save it to file (~170MB) and later load it before shinyServer().
The user can then simply pick the dataset from the list. As the list is already loaded subsetting the list will be very fast for all the users.

Option 2:
Load just the dataset the user asked for
weather.data1, weather.data2,... weather.data2500
Each of these when saved to file are ~70KB. These are then loaded inside shinyServer().

Which of these are better if the shiny app is to be hosted on shinyapps.io.
For option2 will the user feel a delay while his specific data is loaded since it is loaded inside shinyServer()

messages.author: 2b46f14139c84304
messages.subject: Re: loading data all at once versus loading on demand for shiny app
parts:
Hi,

with you number of datasets I would create a global list "weather.data" which contains first only the filenames. If a data set is requested then I would load the data frame. Loading 70 KB can not take so long.

Sigbert

messages.author: 68ce5dd269fd758c
messages.subject: Re: loading data all at once versus loading on demand for shiny app
parts:
I suggest you choose the option 2. 
My reason is: no user will check all the 2500 files, most of them may only check less than 250, so 90% of the data is not necessary. 

For option 2, there will be not long delay, I guess less than 3 seconds.
